prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset: one ORIGINAL MASTER painting for one Bhagavad Gita verse in a Sanskrit reader. Generate a single square 1:1 image, 2048x2048 or the highest actually supported native square resolution. Consistent series style: refined traditional Indian watercolor and restrained gouache on warm ivory handmade paper; fine organic detail, subtle ochre, sage, dusty terracotta and muted indigo; dignified ancient Indian setting, quiet atmospheric daylight. The image must illustrate THIS VERSE'S ACTUAL MEANING. Read the exact source meaning below; derive a concrete, intelligible scene or a restrained symbolic interpretation of that teaching. Never simply paint an unrelated chariot, generic temple or anonymous landscape. Compose one coherent scene, no collage or infographic. Keep important faces, hands, relationships and narrative objects inside the central 60% of width and central 50% of height, surrounded by ample low-detail sky, ground and paper atmosphere. No important subject cut by an edge. This one master must support portrait/landscape phones and tablets through safe proportional fitting. No text of any kind, no verse number, no letters, no Sanskrit/Roman typography, no watermark, no frame, no UI. Text will be rendered separately by the app over the image at a user-adjustable default image opacity of 48%. If Krishna is depicted, maintain a youthful calm blue-skinned figure in muted golden-yellow garments, a restrained peacock-feather crown, no modern jewelry. Arjuna is a dark-haired warrior with a small crown, bow and understated bronze armor. Use them only when the meaning warrants them; the scene or analogy remains verse-specific.  Reference (DO NOT DRAW THIS TEXT): Bhagavad Gītā 2.5. Exact Sanskrit: गुरूनहत्वा हि महानुभावान्
श्रेयो भोक्तुं भैक्ष्यमपीह लोके ।
हत्वार्थकामांस्तु गुरूनिहैव
भुञ्जीय भोगान् रुधिरप्रदिग्धान् ॥ ५ ॥ Exact stored meaning: It is better in this world to beg for sustenance than to kill these great and noble teachers. If I slay them, all the pleasures I would enjoy here would be stained with blood. Chapter context: Arjuna is distressed; Krishna teaches the Self, endurance, wise action and steadiness. For a described analogy, make that exact analogy the image. For abstract Self teachings, use a restrained interpretive natural scene or Krishna quietly instructing Arjuna; no invented literal body of the incorporeal Self. Previous verse context only, do not substitute for the target: Arjuna said: O Madhusudana, O destroyer of enemies, how shall I fight in battle against Bhishma and Drona — who are worthy of my reverence — with arrows? Next verse context only, do not substitute for the target: We do not know which is better for us — that we should conquer them or that they should conquer us. The sons of Dhritarashtra stand before us; having slain them, we would not wish to live. Final instruction: center the distinctive content of the TARGET meaning, not the neighboring verses. No fabricated teaching or unrelated religious scene.
review_note: Contact-sheet inspection; conservative full-frame safe region preserves all figures and objects.

entry.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 2.5: It is better in this world to beg for sustenance than to kill these great and noble teachers. If I slay them, all the pleasures I would enjoy here would be stained with blood.
